question.text: Ms. Lakshmi Raman, an investment manager, is structuring 'Tapti Growth AIF' for a mix of Indian family offices and a group of Singapore-based investors. Which structure pools commitments from domestic and foreign investors into a single onshore SEBI-registered AIF, with foreign investors permitted under the automatic FDI route?

answer.text: Pure offshore - domicile fund in Singapore, register as FVCI with SEBI.
Pure domestic - only Indian investors allowed.
Unified onshore AIF in India - domestic and foreign commitments are pooled into the onshore AIF, with foreign investors permitted under the automatic FDI route.
Four parallel funds in four different jurisdictions.

explanation.text: The Logic: Per the workbook (page 105), a Unified Structure pools commitments from domestic and offshore investors into a single onshore SEBI-registered AIF, with foreign investment permitted under the automatic FDI route. Where an offshore fund is used as a vehicle for the foreign investors, that offshore fund invests in the onshore AIF as one investor alongside the domestic investors. This is the workbook's textbook example of cross-border pooling at the onshore level. The Trap: A pure-offshore design excludes domestic LPs. A pure-domestic design excludes the Singapore investors. Four parallel funds across multiple jurisdictions are over-engineered for the simple two-investor-group scenario and are not what the workbook describes as the unified design. Note: Per page 106, in the offshore-fund variant both the offshore fund and the onshore AIF have their respective investment managers, who are paid management and performance fees at their respective levels. Operational simplicity and Singapore tax certainty are not source-supported claims and should not be treated as inherent to the unified structure.
